record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: What are the values of the abelian repetitive threshold ART(n) and the dual abelian repetitive threshold DART(r)?

evidence.quote: What are the values of ART(n) and DART(r)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer alphabet size $n \geq 2$, an abelian $\alpha$-power is a nonempty word $w$ that can be factorized as $w = u_1 u_2 \cdots u_k v$, where $k \geq 2$, the factors $u_1,\dots,u_k$ are pairwise abelian-equivalent (each is a permutation of the letters of the others), $v$ is a (possibly empty) prefix of an abelian-equivalent permutation of $u_1$, and $\alpha = |w|/|u_1|$. An infinite word over an $n$-letter alphabet is said to avoid abelian $\alpha$-powers if it contains no factor that is an abelian $\beta$-power with $\beta \geq \alpha$. Define the abelian repetitive threshold
$$\mathrm{ART}(n) = \inf\{\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}_{\geq 1} : \text{there exists an infinite word over an } n\text{-letter alphabet avoiding abelian powers of exponent} > \alpha\}.$$

Dually, for a real parameter $r \geq 1$, define the dual abelian repetitive threshold $\mathrm{DART}(r)$ as the least integer $n$ (alphabet size) such that there exists an infinite word over an $n$-letter alphabet avoiding all abelian powers of exponent strictly greater than $r$.

Determine the exact value of $\mathrm{ART}(n)$ for every integer $n \geq 2$, and determine the exact value of $\mathrm{DART}(r)$ for every real $r \geq 1$.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact values of ART(n) remain unknown. Samsonov and Shur (2012) established lower bounds ART(2) ≥ 11/3, ART(3) ≥ 2, ART(4) ≥ 9/5, and ART(k) ≥ (k-2)/(k-3) for k ≥ 5, conjectured to be tight. A 2021/2022 work ("Abelian Repetition Threshold Revisited") showed these lower bounds are not tight for k ∈ {6,7,8,9,10}, leaving exact values open. No exact determination of DART has been published.

status_evidence.title: On abelian repetition threshold
status_evidence.snippet: Samsonov and Shur establish lower bounds for ART(k) and conjecture them tight.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bounds for ART(n) known but exact values unproven.

status_evidence.title: Abelian Repetition Threshold Revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Shows the Samsonov-Shur lower bounds are not tight for k=6,7,8,9,10, refuting the tightness conjecture and leaving exact values of ART open.
status_evidence.claim: Exact values of ART(n) remain undetermined.
